name: United Microelectronics Corporation
blurb: United Microelectronics Corporation (NYSE: UMC; TWSE: 2303) is the world's second-largest pure-play semiconductor foundry, headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan. Unlike TSMC, UMC does not pursue leading-edge nodes; instead it specialises in mature-process technologies from 28nm down to legacy nodes, plus a growing portfolio of specialty processes including silicon photonics, embedded non-volatile memory, and high-voltage CMOS. This positioning makes UMC a direct beneficiary of industrial, automotive, and IoT demand that does not require cutting-edge transistor density.
recent: UMC reported Q4 2025 revenue of NT$61.8 billion (up 4.5% sequentially), with its 22nm node reaching a record 13% of quarterly revenue. Management entered 2026 expecting wafer-pricing increases later in the year, driven by tightening mature-node capacity. The company opened a new 22nm fab in Singapore (Phase 1) targeting 30,000 wafers per month at full ramp, with US$5 billion committed to the site through full build-out. CAPEX guidance for 2026 stands at US$1.5 billion.
